open_points.subject: random identifiers for entity records
open_points.text: `trial_execution_id` M07, `binding_id` M11, `run_id` M19, `approval_id` M24 and `grant_id` M25 are minted at random by the kernel; one that already exists is minted again.
open_points.question: Which module owns random identifier generation, collision detection and reminting for records created by `functions`, `bindings`, `runs` and `effects`?
options: `store` mints identifiers atomically while writing each record
A shared lower-level identifier capability mints them and `store` checks uniqueness
Each record-owning module mints identifiers and retries after a `store` collision
open_points.default_guess: Have `store` mint each random identifier atomically because it alone can check persisted uniqueness in the creation transaction.

open_points.subject: stored payload handoff to execution adapters
open_points.text: `service_invoker` owns building one HTTP request from a binding, the selected instance and the node's inputs; `sandbox` owns every execution of agent code; their `Knows` lists omit `store`, while `store.read_value_bytes` is the capability that returns the bytes a StoredValue or SpooledFile names.
open_points.question: Which module dereferences StoredValue, trial-fixture and SpooledFile references and supplies their actual values or bytes to `sandbox.execute_function` and `service_invoker.prepare_request`, especially after restart when only records remain?
options: `functions`, `runs` and `effects` read through `store` and pass complete in-memory payloads to the adapters
`sandbox` and `service_invoker` may know `store` and dereference records themselves
A separate payload-reading capability sits between `store` and both adapters
open_points.default_guess: Make the calling domain module read through `store` and pass complete payloads to the adapter, preserving the stated `Knows` lists.

open_points.subject: credential-safe process logging
open_points.text: The kernel never puts [a credential] into ... a log line ...; no module section owns process logging or states that runtime logging is absent.
open_points.question: Which module or invariant owns all log emission and ensures that credentials seen by `installation` and `service_invoker` can never enter a log line?
options: `surface` owns one logging capability used by every module and sanitizes all entries
Logging is forbidden in the kernel runtime
Each module that can see a credential independently owns the no-log rule
open_points.default_guess: Forbid runtime logging of request and credential-bearing data, with `surface` owning any bounded operational diagnostics.
